The camera never fully rests in the UI part: slow drifts (0.03-0.12% W per frame) run between moves and turn into the whips; motion runs leftward through four cuts (f1196, f1487, f1542, f1644), so the UI part reads as one continuous camera travel.

Helper scripts besides track.py are in scratch/v7c2_tools/ (eccchain.py whole-frame similarity chain, phasechain.py translation chain, iconr3.py ring radius, blurest*.py Gaussian blur, hblur*.py horizontal blur, pill.py capsule size, wordtimes2.py / promptwords.py word timing, selgrid.py selection order, movers.py difference blobs, framestats.py frame differences, zoomdof.py / edgeprof.py edge width and detail through the footage zoom).
Footage content is not described; the footage motion f1005-f1078 is not analysed. The player's speaker icon is ignored.

Excluded (rule 1): the zoom-in of the footage at f746-f766, recorded in an earlier pass as v7.footage-punch-in-blur with the curve v7.footage-punch-in-blur.v7c2, is a camera move inside the footage, not a scale of the footage layer done in the edit; the technique, its curve (dropped from curves/) and the P1 movement row were removed. A scale in the edit multiplies every blur width by the scale factor, whatever the source resolution; here a horizontal background edge that rises over 4.6 px (10-90%) at f741 (x 900-960, y 371-376) is 88-101 px wide once the zoom has stopped (f769-f790, x5.38-x5.48), 3.5-4.1x more than such a scale allows (about 25 px). A blur added to the whole layer that wide (Gaussian sigma about 33-38 px) would cap gradients at about 3 luma per px, yet the same pictures keep gradients up to 22-32 luma per px (99.9th percentile 13-14, against 8.7 for f741 warped by the measured zoom; top 680 rows, no overlays): the extra blur is local, so the depth of field changes (scratch/v7c2_tools/zoomdof.py -> scratch/v7c2_zoom_dof.csv, scratch/v7c2_tools/edgeprof.py; stills type/v7c2-S01cap_f00741.png, type/v7c2-S01cap_f00790.png). Consecutive pictures stay aligned by a similarity (ECC 0.98-0.99) with a smooth per-picture zoom whose fixed point holds at 64-66% W through f764, so no picture replacement is hidden in the blur. Captions and badge are unaffected.

The f1196 whip-in (incoming half of the first leftward whip) is stored as its own curve v7.trans-whip-push-left-2.v7c2 (template track scratch/v7c2_whip_in_1196_tmpl.csv; the earlier samples scratch/v7c2_whip_in_1196.csv and the disc track scratch/review_v7c2_disc.csv give the same progress within 0.01 and springs {165.8, 27.95} / {161.9, 26.07}); its easing differs from the f1487 instance, so the whip has two incoming variants (probably two techniques).
